What to expect in 422

Developing the scaffolding needed for understanding and building on one’s existing data visualization skills.

  • Aspects
    • Translating data and the relationships within visually for others.
    • Learning to structure and organize data for effective visualization.
    • Learning about the different types of visual representation and their purposes.
    • Understanding of Graphical Perception/perceived visual information and some of the cognitive principles involved.
    • Learning to generate static and interactive visualizations
    • Knowing how to present your visualizations in different media (print, website, video)

What to expect

  • The Process (this makes more sense later)
    • Start with an audience and an idea and find the data (not necessarily in that order)
    • Prepare the data for visualization (e.g., clean, pivot)
    • Represent the data visually with various graphical elements (e.g., color, sizes, and shape)
    • Post-process the data (e.g., decide whether interactivity would add power, post process a static visualization )
  • Tools
    • R/ggplot2, Shiny; Python/matplotlib, Streamlit; Tableau

What is not covered

  • What Stats 422 will not cover
    • JavaScript
    • HTML5
    • CSS
    • Big Data
    • Spark-based viz libraries
  • If any of you know a pro (someone paid to work with these regularly), I could arrange for a stipend if they want to come in as a guest speaker

Story Telling

A story

  • Please let me tell you a story about a former student

What makes a story?

  • “(stories) fulfill a profound human need to grasp the patterns of living not merely as an intellectual exercise, but within a very personal, emotional experience” - Robert McGee (2003 Harvard Business Review)

Story Elements

  • Tension. A problem.
  • Believable and Relatable.
  • A pivot (turning point)
  • A resolution (positive, genuine)
  • Reflection maybe Action

An Outline to close out tonight

  • GOAL: connect your ideas/analyses to your audience’s emotion
    • Suggested (422) solution: tell a compelling story about your visualization
    • Stories allow us to weave a lot of information into whatever we are presenting
    • and allows you to connect to your audience’s emotions and energy.
  • THIS IS NOT EASY TO DO! (don’t give up, practice makes perfect)

An Outline to close out tonight (cont’d)

  • REQUIREMENTS:
  • An understanding of your material
  • Storytelling skills to present ideas that connect with your audience

An Outline to close out tonight (cont’d)

  • RESULT:
    • Your ideas are REMEMBERED.

A data visualization with a story

  • stories often center on life as it is/was and its patterns of change

Categories of Data Viz stories

  • There are plenty, to name a few:
    • illustrate change
    • communicate understanding
    • purely descriptive
    • offers solutions to a problem
  • Neuroscientists tell us we forget bullet points, but we remember stories.

What’s the story? (example)

Some applicable situations

  • We could identify some situations where Data Viz storytelling might apply:
    • Convincing your committee your model is the best model
    • Persuading your employer to apply your recommender system
    • Explaining to a prospective employer the visualization you created for the interview
    • Highlighting problems, finding something of interest (possible solution?)

Reassurance

  • There is NO expectation of perfection in Stats 422
  • Generating data visualizations has a learning curve
  • Even if you use AI

Strategic Storytelling with Data Visualization

  • Keep it simple
  • Edit ruthlessly
  • Be genuine
  • Don’t communicate for yourself — communicate for your audience
  • The story you are telling is not for you; the story is for the audience
  • Help your audience see what you see in the data

More on the Audience

  • Always keep your audience in mind. Give them a reason for spending time with you
  • Think about what will resonate with them and motivate them
  • Also think about whether and when a visualization will strengthen your story
  • Make the information presented specific and relevant to your audience

Advice for Data Visualizations & their stories

  • Even a beautiful data visualization might fail if it does not possess a compelling story/narrative
  • A strong story will overcome a weak data visualization
  • Aim to display data in such a way that makes the complex clear
  • THE IDEAL - when effective visuals are combined with a powerful story

Tactical advice

  • If someone were to only read the label and title of your data visualization, they should still know what it was about
  • All information presented should be self-reinforcing. The content reinforces the titles. The words reinforce the visual
  • Avoid extra or unrelated information, what to drop is as important as what to keep.
  • Try outcome based story development (start with the takeaway and work backwards)
  • Ask others to comment/give feedback
